summary:
Step 8's CODE is clean and I found nothing left to fix in it. I re-verified the two things the re-review was pointed at: (a) the mandated grep over the four code files (`At least|at least|lower bound|LOWER BOUND`) returns exactly the four permitted survivors — Tools/semantic_store.ML:1907 and Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1744 (the two per-theory §12 #12 comment sites), semantic_interpretation.py:1651 (the per-theory clause of the `dry_run` docstring), and the unrelated measurement remark at semantic_store.ML:1994; no cone-level site says "lower bound" any more; (b) the eff* wall mechanism the user's 2026-09-12 ruling rests on is exactly as described in the code (`_contrib`'s wall test at semantic_interpretation.py:1140, the UNCHANGED write of `interpreted_at` at :1384, the scan's staleness test at :1720), and the cone-level comments at Tools/interpret_command.ML:95-100 and Tools/semantic_store.ML:60-64 state "more … or fewer … exact at zero", which is true of that code.

What is NOT yet met is criterion 3 (documentation truth), in three places, all prose, no code, no user-visible string. They form one cluster: the user's DOC-1 ruling was swept through §5.2, §11's first metering bullet, §12, `CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md`'s glossary/§8/§14/caller table and every code comment, but three stragglers were missed, and one of them re-introduces an inconsistency.

(1) fixes-r2-DOC1-A — FIX (minor). Three sites assert an UNQUALIFIED per-theory lower bound and then, one clause later, say the cone sum is neither bound. Those two cannot both hold: if count(T) <= live(T) for every theory T, summing gives that the cone total is a lower bound. The judge's round-one rationale named the surviving property with the qualifier "per theory AT ONE STORE STATE every counted seed is sent"; the applied text dropped "at one store state". The same change set states it correctly at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:753, so the documentation contradicts itself.

(2) fixes-r2-DOC1-B — FIX (major, user's call). Decision row D7 (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:101) was skipped by the sweep and still says the number is "**a lower bound** on the run's work" and "is shown to the user as \"at least n\" (§12)". §12 #8–#11 (:872-882) were re-approved on 2026-09-12 to say "About", and all four code sites emit "About" (Tools/interpret_command.ML:139, semantics.py:1878, :1890, :1929). The authoritative decisions table therefore names a user-visible string that no site emits, and the round-one judge's DOC-1 fix item (4) named D7 by hand.

(3) fixes-r2-P11 — FIX (minor). §11:837-839 still instructs the implementer to restate the proof-channel de-duplication comment on the premise "or n stops being a lower bound"; the code (Tools/semantic_store.ML:2240-2243) correctly says "or n overstates the seed set". The instruction is the half carrying the retired claim, and §11's neighbouring bullet (:826-831) was updated this round while this one was missed.

(4) truth-dryrun-T2 — REJECTED, and named as nitpicking. It is self-defeating and it re-raises two settled rulings.

The remaining work is three hand edits to prose, with the replacement wording fully prescribed below, plus the user's word on D7.

rulings.title: "Exact at zero" is false at the two per-theory §12 #12 comment sites
rulings.rationale:
Rejected on three independent grounds; I verified the decisive one myself rather than taking either party's word.

(a) It is self-defeating. The finding reads the approved sentence ACROSS store states (the dry run at one state; the live run scanned by schedule_dag after ancestors' writes) and concludes that under that reading "Exact at zero" fails per theory while "A LOWER BOUND" survives. That asymmetry does not exist. I re-ran the arithmetic of the round-one judge's own confirmed counterexample against the code on disk: dp(v10/ia10) -> d(v2/ia2) -> E(v3/ia3) in three theories. The dry run counts E in E's theory, because eff*(E)=10 > interpreted_at(E)=3 (semantic_interpretation.py:1719-1720). Live, d's UNCHANGED verdict writes interpreted_at(d) := eff* = 10 (:1384); `_contrib(d, e=10)` then returns ver=2 because `ver > 0 and ia > 0 and e <= ia` holds (:1136-1140); eff*(E) = 3, not > 3, so E is not a seed and E's own theory sends 0. Dry 1 / live 0 IN ONE THEORY — the per-theory lower bound broken by exactly the mechanism the finding invokes against the zero clause. So the cross-state reading falsifies the whole sentence, not one clause of it, and there is exactly one reading under which the approved sentence is true: the per-theory seed set against the store state THAT scan read. Under that reading all three clauses hold — I checked "exact at zero" in both directions at one store state: with no seed no gate runs, so `_propagate` (:1399-1419) can enrol nothing and 0 is sent; and a send requires a seed, so 0 sent implies 0 counted.

(b) The proposed relocation makes it worse on the finding's own terms. Moving "Exact at zero" out of `dry_run_payload` would leave "A LOWER BOUND on the live run's work" there, which is false under the very reading the finding adopts (point a), and would ship the zero clause to the two cone-level comments that already carry it verbatim (Tools/semantic_store.ML:63-64, Tools/interpret_command.ML:99). One falsehood swapped for another, plus a duplicate.

(c) It re-raises settled rulings and re-escalates approved text. judge.json's elegance-S8-2 settled the placement of the verbatim §12 #12 text at the per-theory site ("a placement error, not a request to reword approved text"), and docs-DOC-1's rationale settled the truth question in the same document with the words "the per-theory §12 #12 comment is true as written". DOC-1 was routed discuss_with_user, the user ruled on 2026-09-12, and that ruling deliberately left #12 where it now sits. Asking for the approved sentence to be re-put to the user is precisely what SCOPE.md:142-143 names as nitpicking to be rejected harshly. Its fallback (add "against the store state this scan saw" to the neighbouring non-approved lines) describes no failure and duplicates a qualifier already present at semantic_interpretation.py:1651.
rulings.fix: No edit. The approved §12 #12 sentence stays verbatim at Tools/semantic_store.ML:1905-1910 and Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1743-1747, and the cone-level comments stay as the user's 2026-09-12 ruling left them.

rulings.title: Decision row D7 was missed by the DOC-1 sweep: it still says "a lower bound" and "shown to the user as 'at least n' (§12)"
rulings.rationale:
Confirmed on disk, and the falsehood is checkable in one line. SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:101 reads `| D7 | The dry run returns one number per theory, **a lower bound** on the run's work: the seed set's size (§5.2); it serves the two existing `n = 0` guards and the 400 threshold, and is shown to the user as "at least n" (§12) |`. But §12 of the same file now carries the 2026-09-12 re-approved texts and all four say "About" (#8 at :872-874, #9 at :876-877, #10 at :879-880, #11 at :882), and the shipped code agrees with §12 at every site: Tools/interpret_command.ML:139, Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:1878, :1890, :1929. So the decisions table — the authoritative index of what the user settled — names a user-visible string that no site emits.

This is not an omission the re-review may waive. judge.json's docs-DOC-1 fix item (4) names D7 by hand. The user ruled on 2026-09-12 and the ruling was carried into §5.2 (:239-247), §11's first metering bullet (:829-830), §12 (:872-882) and the parent design (CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:39, :431-435, :469, the last even carrying the dated marker). Every sibling site was swept; D7 alone was skipped.

Two qualifications shape the fix. First, the finding's framing that §5.2 and the glossary "cite D7 as the authority" is loose: §5.2 merely heads its paragraph `**Dry run (D7).**` and the parent glossary row cites §5.2, not D7. That does not rescue the row — §2 is authoritative in its own right — but the severity rests on D7's own status. Second, the "lower bound" half of the row is the same defect as DOC1-A, so the two must be repaired with one wording, not two.

This is not re-opening a settled decision: the decision itself (one number per theory = the seed set's size, serving the two `n = 0` guards and the 400 threshold) is untouched; only the row's description is brought into line with the user's own later ruling, exactly as §12 #8–#11 already were. Because it edits a §2 decision row, it goes to the user rather than being applied alone.
rulings.fix:
One hand edit (project rule: no scripted edits to plan documents), replacing SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:101 in full, and using the SAME qualified formulation as the DOC1-A fix so the two do not diverge:

| D7 | The dry run returns one number per theory, the seed set's size (§5.2) — per theory, against the store state that scan read, every counted seed is sent, but summed over a cone **neither bound** (step-8 review, 2026-09-12); it serves the two existing `n = 0` guards (where it is exact) and the 400 threshold, and is shown to the user as "About n" (§12, re-approved 2026-09-12) |

Change nothing else in §2, and nothing in §5.2, §11 or §12 — they already carry the 2026-09-12 ruling. Show the user the replacement row before committing it; the edit is mechanical but the row records their decision.

rulings.title: The DOC-1 fix dropped the judge's "at one store state" qualifier: three sites assert an unqualified per-theory lower bound that the same paragraph refutes
rulings.rationale:
Confirmed on disk, and the decisive argument is arithmetic rather than stylistic, so it clears the no-nitpicking bar.

At each of the three sites the per-theory claim sits in the same sentence as the cone claim, and the two cannot both hold. If count(T) <= live(T) for every theory T of the cone, then summing over T gives that the cone total IS a lower bound. The adjacent clause asserts the opposite. Verified verbatim: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:236-238 "Per theory it is a lower bound on what the live run sends" against :239-244 "Summed over a cone it is **neither bound** … walling off a dependent in the later theory that the dry run had counted"; CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:39 「单个 theory 内是 live run 发送数的下界（依赖者不计），跨锥则**上下界都不是**」; semantic_interpretation.py:1651-1654 "per theory a lower bound on what an ordinary run sends to the LLM … summed over a cone neither bound (an ancestor theory's UNCHANGED verdict can wall off a seed counted here)" — where "here" is the very theory the preceding clause called a lower bound. The walled-off entity was counted in one particular theory, so in that theory count > sends, and the paragraph refutes its own previous sentence. CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:753, written by the same change set, states the property correctly with the qualifier 「单个 theory 内、对同一库状态，数到的种子全部发送」, so the change set says both things.

I checked the obvious rebuttals and none holds. The round-one judge did bless an unqualified per-theory sentence, but only for the approved §12 #12 comment at the two per-theory FUNCTION sites (Tools/semantic_store.ML:1907, semantic_interpretation.py:1744), where nothing in the surrounding text mentions a cone; this finding deliberately does not touch either, so it is neither rewording approved text nor re-raising elegance-S8-2. The earlier phrase "against the store as it stands before the run" describes how the number is COMPUTED, not the basis of the comparison with the live run, and cannot absorb :243-244's explicit statement that the live run does not send a dependent counted in a later theory. And the judge's prescribed fix text for CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:39/:380/:431-434 was "more … or fewer … exact at zero"; the per-theory lower-bound clause was ADDED beyond it, lifted from his rationale's surviving-properties sentence, which carried "at one store state" — precisely the words dropped.

Severity is minor, not major: no code is wrong, no user-visible text is wrong, and §14's acceptance row (CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:750-754), where a test author would work from, already carries the correct qualifier — so the challenger's "an acceptance test asserts live_sent(T) >= dry_count(T) and fails" overstates the reach. What remains is a genuine internal contradiction in the documents whose whole purpose, per DOC-1, is to stop someone asserting an untrue bound.

Routed self_decide_then_rereview rather than to the user: no approved §12 text, no behaviour and no decision row is touched (D7 itself is handled separately under fixes-r2-DOC1-B), and the correct wording already exists verbatim in the same document at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:753.
rulings.fix:
Text only, three sites, no code change; edit both plan documents by hand (project rule: no scripted edits to plan documents).

1. SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:236-238 — replace "Per theory it is a lower bound on what the live run sends (dependents are not counted: …)" with "Per theory, against the store state the dry run read, every counted seed is sent (dependents are not counted: …)". Leave :239-253 alone, including the approved §12 #12 block at :250-253.

2. /home/qiyuan/Current/MLML/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:39 — replace 「单个 theory 内是 live run 发送数的下界（依赖者不计）」 with the wording this same document already uses at :753: 「单个 theory 内、对同一库状态，数到的种子全部发送（依赖者不计）」. The rest of the row (「跨锥则**上下界都不是**…零处精确…"About n"」) stays.

3. Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py:1651 — replace "per theory a lower bound on what an ordinary run sends to the LLM" with "per theory, against the store state this scan read, every counted seed is sent".

Explicitly do NOT touch Tools/semantic_store.ML:1905-1910 or semantic_interpretation.py:1743-1747 (user-approved §12 #12 text, ruled true as written at a per-theory function), nor Tools/semantic_store.ML:54-66 and Tools/interpret_command.ML:95-100 (cone-level comments, already correct).

rulings.title: §11's instruction for the proof-channel de-duplication comment still prescribes the retired "lower bound" premise
rulings.rationale:
Confirmed on disk on both halves. SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:837-839 still reads "must be restated on a premise that survives (\"no uk may be counted twice inside one quote, or n stops being a lower bound\")", while the comment it governs, Tools/semantic_store.ML:2240-2243, now reads "No uk may be counted twice inside one dry run, or n overstates the seed set". Prescription and code state two different premises, and the prescription is the half carrying the retired cone-wide lower bound.

The sentence is not merely stale phrasing: it asserts that the quoted premise is one "that survives", and under the user's 2026-09-12 ruling (transcribed at §5.2:239-244, "Summed over a cone it is **neither bound**") the cone-wide n is not a lower bound at all, so the premise it recommends presupposes a retired property. The implementer plainly agreed in practice — this is one of the three "lower bound / at least" comment remnants round two reworded, and the rewording landed on "or n overstates the seed set".

The natural defence, that §11 is a frozen pre-implementation record like §2's decision rows, fails: round two rewrote the immediately preceding bullet of the SAME §11 list in place (:829-830 now reads "the dry run count is the sum of the seed sets, neither bound over a cone (§5.2), shown as \"About n\""), so §11 is a maintained list in this step and this bullet is the straggler. Nor is it a re-raise: no first-round ruling covers plan :838-839; DOC-1's fix text named §5.2/D7 and the code sites.

In scope under re-review item 2 (every sentence about the dry-run count in the two plan documents must be true of the code). Minor: documentation only, no behavioural effect. Routed self_decide_then_rereview — it is a quotation of a code comment, not approved text and not a decision.
rulings.fix:
By hand (no scripted edits to plan documents), change only the parenthetical at SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:838-839 so it quotes the premise the code actually states:

  from: must be restated on a premise that survives ("no uk may be counted twice inside one quote, or n stops being a lower bound")
  to:   must be restated on a premise that survives ("no uk may be counted twice inside one dry run, or n overstates the seed set")

Nothing else in the bullet: leave its ":2199-2207" line anchor alone (stale line anchors were ruled nitpicking under elegance-S8-6), leave D7 at :101 to fixes-r2-DOC1-B, and change no code — Tools/semantic_store.ML:2240-2243 is the correct half and stays as it is.
